input.content:
# LifeOS Console Run your workspace agents as a **team you chat with in Discord**, locally on your machine. Post a task in a project channel; **Jarvis** (your chief-of-staff orchestrator) opens a thread, delegates to the right agents, and they work **in that thread as themselves** while you watch and jump in. No API key, no public server — everything runs through your Claude **subscription** via the Agent SDK. > Status: built and typecheck-verified. **Not yet run live** — it needs one Discord application per > bot (tokens). Follow *Setup* below to bring it online. --- ## The model - **One bot per role/name — 20 bots.** Shared roles (`architect`, `feature-dev`, `infra-ops`, `qa-verify`) are a single bot each that serves every project; the **project context is resolved by the channel** the bot is working in. The other 16 agents are one bot each. `jarvis` is the orchestrator. - **Channels are project-scoped.** On startup Jarvis creates `#general` + one channel per project. A bot working in `#accessbuddy` runs as that project's overlay; in `#lifesaveroncall`, that one. - **Jarvis is the single front door.** Post a task in a project channel → Jarvis opens a **thread**, triages, and **delegates in dependency phases** (architecture → build → test). Agents in one phase run **in parallel** (the same role can run multiple instances), each posts its work **into the thread under its own name**, and Jarvis summarises. You have oversight in one place and can reply in-thread to steer, or let it run. - **Talk to one agent directly:** `@mention` any bot in a channel/thread, or DM it. - **Gated + autonomous:** read-only tools run freely; edits/shell/delegation/memory-writes prompt **Approve / Always / Deny**. `/autopilot` lets a bot act without asking (destructive/outbound actions and memory writes still confirm). Threads remember across turns (session resume). ### Agent definitions — train a role once ``` ~/Documents/workspace/ _bases//base.md # shared role definition (persona, method, memory protocol) projects//agents// claude.md # overlay: `base: ` + project specifics (or a full def if unique) memory.md # what this agent has learnt context/ # optional agent-specific working files projects//context/*.md # project foundation (read by every agent in the project) personal/agents/jarvis/claude.md # the orchestrator (`orchestrator: true`) ``` A shared role's system prompt is composed as **shared base → project overlay → memory → project context**. Edit `_bases/architect/base.md` once and every project's architect inherits it. Agents are discovered anywhere in the workspace tree (`*/agents//claude.md`). --- ## Setup ### Prerequisites - **bun** (project standard; do not use npm). - A Discord **server** you own. Enable Developer Mode (User Settings → Advanced) to copy IDs. - `DISCORD_GUILD_ID` in `.env` — your server's ID (right-click server → Copy Server ID). ### 1. Create one Discord application per bot Discord has no API to create apps, so this step is manual — **once per bot** (20 of them). For each: 1. https://discord.com/developers/applications → **New Application**. Name it the agent's display name (this name + icon is how it appears in DMs and channels). → Create. 2. *(optional)* **General Information** → upload an icon = the agent's avatar. 3. **Bot** (left) → **Privileged Gateway Intents** → enable **MESSAGE CONTENT INTENT** → Save. *(Required — without it the bot can't read messages.)* 4. **Bot** → **Reset Token** → copy it. > Tip: start with `jarvis` + one or two others to prove the flow before doing all 20. ### 2. Store the tokens Keyed by **bot name** (the role/agent name, e.g. `architect`, `feature-dev`, `jarvis`): - Paste into `code/.data/discord-tokens.json` — `{ "architect": "…", "jarvis": "…", … }`, **or** - set env vars `DISCORD_TOKEN_` (name uppercased, non-alphanumerics → `_`). The repo ships a pre-filled template of all 20 slots (empty) at `.data/discord-tokens.json`. ### 3. Onboard + invite ```bash cd ~/Documents/workspace/projects/life-os-console/code bun install # scaffold a brand-new agent (optional): writes claude.md + memory.md bun run onboard --agent personal/jarvis --token --create --orchestrator --title "Jarvis" # validate every stored token and print an invite URL per bot: bun run onboard --all ``` Open each printed invite URL → choose your server → Authorize. ### 4. Run ```bash bun start # boots the fleet; Jarvis creates #general + project channels on first run bun run typecheck # tsc --noEmit ``` --- ## Using it - **Run a task:** post it in a project channel (e.g. `#accessbuddy`). Jarvis threads it, delegates, and the team works in the thread. Reply in the thread to steer. - **Ad-hoc:** post in `#general` (no project context — for quick/cross-cutting things). - **Talk to one agent:** `@mention` it in any channel/thread, or DM it directly. - **Slash commands (per bot):** `/autopilot` (toggle autonomous mode), `/tasks` (recent tasks). - **Approvals:** gated actions show **Approve / Always (this tool) / Deny** buttons in the thread. State is in `.data/` (gitignored): `discord-tokens.json`, `sessions.json` (thread→session for resume), `autopilot.json`, `tasks.json`. Tune via `.env`: `AGENT_MODEL`, `MAX_TURNS`. --- ## Adding agents - **Another project for an existing role:** create `projects/

/agents//claude.md` with `base: ` + a few project-specific lines, plus `memory.md`. It joins that role's existing bot — no new token needed (the bot resolves it by channel). - **A new role:** add `_bases//base.md`, then per-project overlays. Each new distinct agent name is a new bot → a new Discord app + token slot. Re-run `bun run onboard --all`. --- ## Security - **No API key, no inbound URL.** Auth is your Claude subscription; spawned agents don't load your PAI hooks/settings. Bots connect outbound over the gateway. - **Tokens are secrets.** `.env` and `.data/` are gitignored — never commit or paste tokens elsewhere. If a token is exposed, **Reset Token** in the portal. (The legacy single `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` in `.env` is unused by the fleet — delete it and rotate it.) - **Gates hold under autopilot:** `rm -rf`, `git push`, `sudo`, outbound `POST`, `npm publish`, and memory writes always confirm. --- ## Known limitations - **Not yet live-verified** — built, typechecked, and module-load checked, but no run against real Discord (no tokens). The first live task is the real test. - **Phase ordering is Jarvis-driven, not an enforced DAG.** The delegate tool runs each call's agents in parallel; Jarvis sequences phases (design → build → test) by reasoning + the tool's guidance. - **`#general` is projectless** — a shared role bot there uses its default overlay's context. - **Slack frontend is legacy** (`bun run start:slack`) and is not maintained for this model. --- ## Layout ``` src/ index.ts entrypoint (boots the fleet) discordApp.ts the fleet: bots, channels, threads, Jarvis front door, in-thread delegation roster.ts scans the workspace tree; base+overlay system prompt; getBots() fleet grouping executor.ts runs an agent task via the Agent SDK (resume, ask_user, delegate, memory) delegateTool.ts Jarvis's phase/parallel delegate tool agentConfig.ts per-agent tool policy + cwd approval.ts gated-tool approval handler memoryTool.ts gated update_memory askUserTool.ts ask_user (pause for a free-form reply) sessions.ts thread/DM → SDK session id (resume) autopilot.ts per-bot autonomous mode + always-allow tasks.ts / store.ts / inference.ts / util.ts scripts/ onboard-agent.ts create app token → validate → store → invite URL (--all for batch) ```
